statement: Let G be a connected graph n > 2 vertices. γ_2 ≤ -1 + α*(δ + |Α_1 |), where δ is the minimum degrees and A_1 is the set of vertices that are adjacent to exactly one non-minimum degree vertex.

readings.interpretation: gamma_2 <= -1 + alpha*(delta + |A_1|); A_1 = vertices adjacent to exactly one NON-minimum-degree vertex. Graph is 11-regular so no non-min-degree vertices exist => every vertex has 0 such neighbors => A_1 = empty. Glossary: gamma_2 def 'γ_2', alpha def 'α(G)', delta def 'δ(G)'.
Alternative precedence -1 + alpha*delta + |A_1| (ignoring parenthesization).

notes: Regular graph makes A_1 empty under the natural reading. Holds with slack 17.

statement: If G is a connected graph n > 2 vertices, then γ_2 ≤ [α* ecc_avg(A) + |B| ]/2, where A is the set of minimum degree vertices and B is the set of periphery vertices.

readings.interpretation: gamma_2 <= [alpha*ecc_avg(A) + |B|]/2; A = min-degree vertices = all 20 (regular), ecc_avg(A) = 2 (glossary 'ecc_avg(S)' = average of vertex eccentricities ecc(v) over S; all ecc = 2); B = periphery = all 20 (all ecc equal).
Alternative precedence alpha*ecc_avg(A) + |B|/2.

notes: Vertex-transitive: center = periphery = V. Holds under both precedence readings.

statement: If G is a connected graph n > 2 vertices, then γ_2 ≤ [ diam(G)( α + |X| )]/2, where X is the set of vertices whose local independence is maximum.

readings.interpretation: gamma_2 <= [diam(G)*(alpha + |X|)]/2; X = vertices of maximum local independence. lambda(v) = 2 for all v (glossary 'λ(v)': independence number of G[N(v)]) => X = all 20. diam = 2.

notes: Status-evidence special case diam=2 => gamma_2 <= alpha + |X| = 22 also holds.

statement: If G is a connected graph n > 2 vertices, then γ_2 ≤ Maxine + γ.

readings.interpretation: gamma_2 <= Maxine + gamma. Glossary 'maxine': size of independent set left by greedy max-degree removal = 2 (verified over 200 random tie-breaks; also maxine <= alpha = 2). gamma = 2 (ILP-verified).

notes: TIGHT: holds with equality (4 <= 4). C5[K4] is a sharpness example, not a counterexample. gamma_2=4 double-checked by ILP and by hand (blob-coverage counting argument gives gamma_2 >= 4; {0,1,8,9} is a 2-dominating set).

statement: If G is a connected graph on n > 2 vertices, then γ_2 ≤ FLOOR(n - | Τ | /2 ), where T = {k: some vertex of G has exactly k triangles incident to it}.

readings.interpretation: gamma_2 <= FLOOR(n - |T|/2), T = {k: some vertex has exactly k incident triangles}. T(v) = 39 for all v (vertex-transitive) => T = {39}, |T| = 1. Reading: floor(20 - 1/2) = 19.
Alternative grouping floor((n - |T|)/2).

notes: Holds under both groupings.

statement: If G is a connected graph on n > 2, then γ_2 ≤ n - m + 1. where m is the(upper) median of the degree sequence.

readings.interpretation: gamma_2 <= n - m + 1, m = upper median of degree sequence (glossary 'median(degseq)': n even => upper median = d_{(n+2)/2} = d_11 = 11).

notes: All degrees 11, so any median convention gives 11. Holds with slack 6.

statement: If G is a connected graph on n > 2 vertices, then γ_2 ≤ |M|*(q + | A_2 |) -1, where A_2 is the set vertices of degree at most two, M is the set of vertices of mode_min degree and q is the 1st quartile degree.

readings.interpretation: gamma_2 <= |M|*(q + |A_2|) - 1; M = vertices of mode_min degree (unique mode 11 => all 20), q = 1st quartile degree (glossary 'q1(degseq)': d_{n/4} = d_5 = 11), A_2 = vertices of degree <= 2 = empty.
Alternative precedence |M|*q + |A_2| - 1.

notes: Holds by a huge margin.

statement: If G is a connected graph on n > 2 vertices, then γ_2 ≤ p(G) + 1 + μ(G[T]) + |E(G[A_3 ])|, where T is the set vertices of degree two and A_3 is the set of vertices of degree at least three.

readings.interpretation: gamma_2 <= p(G) + 1 + mu(G[T]) + |E(G[A_3])|; T = degree-2 vertices = empty => mu(G[T]) = 0; A_3 = degree >= 3 vertices = all 20 => E(G[A_3]) = E(G), 110 edges; p(G) = 1 (Hamiltonian, explicit cycle verified).

notes: Holds trivially.

statement: If G is a connected graph on n > 2 vertices, then γ_2 ≤ μ(G[V - A_δ ]) + | A_δ | + |{ v: |N(v) ∩ Α_2 | = 1}|, where A_δ is the set of vertices of minimum degree and A_2 is the set of vertices of degree 2.

readings.interpretation: gamma_2 <= mu(G[V - A_delta]) + |A_delta| + |{v: |N(v) ∩ A_2| = 1}|; regular => A_delta = V, V - A_delta = empty => mu = 0; A_2 (degree-2 vertices) = empty => third term 0.

notes: Regular graph degenerates RHS to n = 20. Holds.

statement: If G is a connected graph on n > 2 vertices, then γ_2 ≤ μ(G[V - A_δ ]) + | A_δ | + κ_v(G), where A_δ is the set of vertices of minimum degree and κ_v is the number of cut vertices.

readings.interpretation: gamma_2 <= mu(G[V - A_delta]) + |A_delta| + kappa_v(G); A_delta = V (regular) => mu term 0; kappa_v = 0 cut vertices (8-connected).

notes: Holds.

statement: If G is a connected graph on n > 2 vertices, then γ_2 ≤ μ(G) + μ(G[V - N(N(P))]) + | A_δ |, where A_δ is the set of vertices of minimum degree and P is the set of pendants.

readings.interpretation: gamma_2 <= mu(G) + mu(G[V - N(N(P))]) + |A_delta|; P = pendants = empty => N(N(P)) = empty => G[V - {}] = G, mu = 10; A_delta = V.

notes: Empty-pendant convention: N(empty) = empty (glossary N(S) = vertices adjacent to at least one vertex of S). Holds under any convention since |A_delta| = 20 alone exceeds gamma_2.

statement: If G is a connected graph on n > 2 vertices, then γ_2 ≤ μ(G) + μ(G[N(A_2 )]) + | A_δ |, where A_δ is the set of vertices of minimum degree and A_2 is the set vertices of degree two.

readings.interpretation: gamma_2 <= mu(G) + mu(G[N(A_2)]) + |A_delta|; A_2 = degree-2 vertices = empty => N(A_2) = empty, mu = 0; A_delta = V.

notes: Holds.

notes: Tightest of the 39x family here (slack 6) but holds.

notes: K_4 per-vertex count computed exactly (345 total K_4's, 69 per vertex). Holds.
